# Unit test for function compare
def test_compare():
    # Test with typical positive integers
    assert compare([1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]) == [3, 3, 3]
    assert compare([1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3]) == [0, 0, 0]

    # Test with single element lists
    assert compare([5], [10]) == [5]

    # Test with negative numbers
    assert compare([-1, -2, -3], [-4, -5, -6]) == [3, 3, 3]
    assert compare([-1, 2, -3], [4, -5, 6]) == [5, 7, 9]

    # Test with mixed positive and negative
    assert compare([10, -10], [-10, 10]) == [20, 20]

    # Test with zeros
    assert compare([0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0]) == [0, 0, 0]
    assert compare([0], [5]) == [5]

    # Test with empty lists
    assert compare([], []) == []

    # Test with larger differences
    assert compare([100, 200], [1, 2]) == [99, 198]

    # Test result type and length
    result = compare([1, 2], [3, 4])
    assert isinstance(result, list)
    assert len(result) == 2

    # Test all elements are non-negative
    result = compare([1, 5, 10], [10, 1, 5])
    assert all(x >= 0 for x in result)
    assert result == [9, 4, 5]
